I am a woman of 47 years in the North East, and beans is what I plant on this small plot near the house. I have no schooling, but my mother and my husband's people taught me how to grow cowpea and groundnut, and I keep the seeds from last harvest to plant again. Money is tight and fertilizer price is high, so I put small small on the cereal plots, not on beans — beans feed the soil themselves. I will weed by hand with my daughters, and if the insects come heavy on the flowers I will buy one small bottle of chemical from the market to spray, because without that the pods will be empty.
